_golden: GOLDEN REFERENCE (arc problem-solution: software, SaaS, science, finance). Study it, then write YOUR product's film from YOUR docs. Do not copy its lines, its numbers or its product. It is not buildable (no materials). Every _why says what a top crew did and why.
_facts: The docs this film was written from (fictional product): Margin — invoicing for freelance translators. Drop in the source file and Margin counts the words (DOCX, PDF, XLIFF) and prices the job at your rate per word. Invoices in 31 currencies. Reminds the client on day 14 and day 30 if unpaid. From source file to sent invoice takes under a minute (timed on 50 real jobs). Exports a year of invoices as one CSV for your tax return. 9 euros a month. Made by two translators in Lisbon.

_anchors.proposition: Translators should spend their evenings on words, not on invoices.
_anchors.concept: The last page — the job ends with an invoice nobody wants to write
_anchors.hook: The translation took a week. The invoice took the evening.
_anchors.hero: Finish the work. Not the paperwork.
_anchors.last: The translation takes a week. The invoice takes a minute.
_anchors._why: Hook, hero and last line are written FIRST and say the concept three times in three ways. The last line calls back to the hook word for word, with one change: that change is the product.

title.en: Reminders you don't have to send

scenes._why: The breath: no picture, one line, no new fact. It names the feeling under the proposition. Two dense beats, then one calm beat.
Only numbers that are in the docs. Three at most; the voice says none of them (the screen does).

The hero at ~65 %: one real result screen (the invoice, sent) pushes in, then settles above the tagline. The work, done, is the hero; a wall of every screen would say nothing. The tagline is the proposition in five words.
